subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Power of Shorter Meetings
description: A 60-second lesson on The Power of Shorter Meetings.

hook.text: Parkinson's Law states that work expands to fill the time available. A 60-minute slot fills 60 minutes of talk.

buildup.text: Calendar tools default to 30 or 60 minutes. This arbitrary standard shapes every meeting's length.

discovery.text: A 25-minute meeting replaces a 30-minute meeting with a built-in transition buffer and sharper focus.

twist.text: Fifteen-minute meetings sound impossible until you try one with a clear agenda. Constraint breeds efficiency.

climax.text: Default to 25 or 50 minutes. The five-minute gap prevents back-to-back meeting fatigue and late starts.

punchline.text: Shorter defaults. Tighter focus. Built-in breaks.

quiz.question: Why should meetings default to 25 or 50 minutes instead of 30 or 60?
options: It saves money on conference room bookings
The gap prevents fatigue and late starts while sharpening focus
People can only pay attention for odd-numbered durations
